result:
Lane finished. PR #197 is ready, CI green on `0781ab898b`.

## What attempt 1 left, and what this one did

Attempt 1 had registered the falsifier and queued only the two arms needing no driver swap; both had landed unscored, and `t26`/`stock` were never queued. So the experiment's answer didn't exist. I scored the existing T30 runs (no device time re-spent) and ran the missing four arms.

## The answer: refuted

Six soaks on the thor, one ref and one apk, two runs per arm, each arm labelled from the driver string in its own frame dump:

| arm | driver (from the dump) | `R_full` | `R_lower` |
|---|---|---|---|
| t30 | PurpleVK 26.3.0 | 9.5, 5.4 | 23.8, 16.3 |
| t26 | PurpleVK 26.1.0 | 5.1, 8.4 | 15.4, 22.9 |
| stock | Qualcomm Adreno 69e13475cb | 4.8, 9.2 | 20.2, 23.7 |

No arm has both runs outside the band on the same side. The largest gap between two arms' means is **0.70** per 100 against a smallest *within-arm* difference of **3.3** — the driver moves the rate less than re-running the same driver does. Sensitivity as pre-registered: 2 se of an arm-vs-T30 difference is 7.9 per 100, 88% of the T30 mean, so this excludes an effect the size of the artifact and no smaller. It does not say the effect is zero.

The control arm corrected its own pre-registration: `t30-2` fell below both registered bands, widening the same-driver spread in the direction that makes a positive result harder. PR #165's "`R_lower` is the more sensitive region" is withdrawn.

## The finding worth more than the null

**The artifact fires on Qualcomm's proprietary Adreno driver** at the same rate. Two Mesa builds two releases apart plus an independent vendor implementation all produce it, so #77 is not a Turnip bug — it is in what we hand the driver. That also closes the earlier void A/B: T26 and stock *do* show it; that verdict was the 180 s soak, exactly as `blocked_on` said.

## Two defects found on the way

- Both stock runs first scored `driver: ?` — Adreno's version string has embedded newlines, so a stock session header spans five JSONL lines. My own guard G2 voids a run on an unparseable header, so a reader bug was one step from being published as "the stock arm produced no readable run". The instrument failed on the only arm whose label carried information. Fixed, tested both directions, both mutants confirmed to trip.
- `swap_driver.sh` is unguarded out-of-band device state and defaults to the *Nova's* serial while this experiment is on the thor. I pinned my soaks, kept the windows short, and audited them after: 4 runs in 21 minutes of exposure, all mine. Clean by luck as much as design.

**One thing I could not do:** `preflight.sh --allow-tracker` fails its coverage gate on **#200**, an unrelated open issue with neither a lane nor a `blocked_on`. All three remedies are edits to board files a lane may not make, and `--allow-tracker` doesn't cover that gate. It's stated in the PR body and in the board request I filed at `dispatch/board-requests/drvab77.md`, which also asks for `issue.77`'s `blocked_on` to be cleared.
